plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (Ge/ZnS Fabry-Perot dual-bandpass) based on prior iteration evidence. Iteration 05 achieved 0.978 target score with broad initialization, while iteration 09's quarter-wave seeded approach scored only 0.383, suggesting over-constrained initialization. Three complementary refinement routes: (1) increase layer count to 24 for more cavity degrees of freedom, (2) test alternative IR material pair (ZnSe/ZnS) with lower absorption, (3) implement explicit 3-cavity topology with analytical quarter-wave seeding but relaxed ±25% bounds. All routes preserve CaF2 substrate, normal incidence, dual passband requirements, and 24-layer maximum constraint.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot Dual-Bandpass with 24 Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 24 enables three Fabry-Perot cavities instead of two, providing additional degrees of freedom to simultaneously optimize both passbands (4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm) while maintaining stopband suppression (3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm).
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with alternating high/low index quarter-wave stacks forming three resonant cavities, optimized via gradient-based thickness tuning with quarter-wave analytical initialization.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | (Ge/ZnS) periodic Bragg mirrors | 3 cavity spacers | (Ge/ZnS) periodic Bragg mirrors | air, exactly 24 finite layers total
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition: 2nd = mλ for constructive interference
Bragg mirror reflectivity increases with layer pair count
Multi-cavity coupling produces squarer passband profiles
expected_advantages: More cavity degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
Higher stopband suppression with additional mirror pairs
known_risks: Increased total thickness may cause stress issues
More layers increase fabrication tolerance sensitivity
Optimization may converge to local minima
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band infrared transmission. Layer sequence: Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS (24 finite layers, alternating Ge and ZnS starting with Ge). Wavelength bands: passbands at 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm (maximize transmittance), stopbands at 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm (minimize transmittance). Normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent TMM. Initialize all Ge layers at 550 nm and all ZnS layers at 900 nm (quarter-wave at 4.4 μm center). Optimization bounds: Ge [400, 700] nm, ZnS [650, 1150] nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with learning rate 0.002, clamp thickness changes to ±15% of nominal values for first 3 epochs, then release full bounds. Maximum 500 optimization iterations. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Increased layer count from 20 to 24 to enable three-cavity topology, addressing iteration 09's poor performance (0.383 score) by providing more optimization degrees of freedom while retaining quarter-wave initialization principle from feedback directives.

routes.title: ZnSe/ZnS Alternative Material Pair Dual-Bandpass with 20 Layers
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing Ge with ZnSe as the high-index material will reduce absorption losses in the 4-5 μm range while maintaining sufficient index contrast with ZnS, potentially improving peak transmittance and reducing thermal emission background.
routes.design_principle: Same two-cavity Fabry-Perot topology as iteration 05 but with ZnSe/ZnS material pair instead of Ge/ZnS, leveraging lower absorption coefficient of ZnSe in mid-IR.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | (ZnSe/ZnS) periodic Bragg mirrors | 2 cavity spacers | (ZnSe/ZnS) periodic Bragg mirrors | air, exactly 20 finite layers total
manufacturing_considerations: ZnSe and ZnS are both conventional IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Material absorption coefficient directly affects maximum achievable transmittance
Index contrast determines mirror reflectivity and cavity finesse
ZnSe has lower extinction coefficient than Ge in 4-5 μm range
expected_advantages: Reduced thermal emission from filter itself
Better long-term stability in harsh environments
known_risks: ZnSe/ZnS index contrast may be lower than Ge/ZnS, requiring more layers for same stopband
ZnSe is more expensive and may have different stress properties
Material optical constants must be verified for target wavelength range
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band infrared transmission. Layer sequence: ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS-ZnSe-ZnS (20 finite layers, alternating ZnSe and ZnS starting with ZnSe). Wavelength bands: passbands at 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm (maximize transmittance), stopbands at 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm (minimize transmittance). Normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent TMM. Initialize all ZnSe layers at 600 nm and all ZnS layers at 950 nm (quarter-wave at 4.4 μm center). Optimization bounds: ZnSe [450, 750] nm, ZnS [700, 1200] nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with learning rate 0.002, clamp thickness changes to ±15% of nominal values for first 3 epochs, then release full bounds. Maximum 500 optimization iterations. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Tests alternative material pair hypothesis while preserving 20-layer topology from iteration 05 (which achieved 0.978 score). Addresses feedback directive to anchor initialization while exploring whether material choice rather than topology limits performance.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity with Relaxed Quarter-Wave Bounds (20 Layers)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Iteration 09's poor performance (0.383 score) resulted from over-constrained quarter-wave initialization with ±40% bounds. Relaxing to ±25% bounds around analytical quarter-wave targets while enforcing strict layer alternation will provide better optimization convergence than either broad initialization (iteration 05) or tight quarter-wave seeding (iteration 09).
routes.design_principle: Two-cavity Fabry-Perot with quarter-wave analytical initialization but relaxed optimization bounds (±25% instead of ±40%), combined with enforced alternation constraints and reduced learning rate per feedback directives.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | (Ge/ZnS) periodic Bragg mirrors | 2 cavity spacers | (Ge/ZnS) periodic Bragg mirrors | air, exactly 20 finite layers total
design_variables: all 20 layer thicknesses with alternation constraint
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks provide analytical starting point for Fabry-Perot design
Optimization bound width affects convergence speed and final solution quality
Learning rate reduction prevents overshooting in narrow optimization basins
expected_advantages: Better convergence than iteration 09's tight bounds
More physically meaningful initialization than iteration 05's uniform 500 nm
Enforced alternation prevents optimizer from breaking layer sequence
known_risks: May still underperform compared to iteration 05's broad initialization
Learning rate reduction may slow convergence
Alternation constraint may prevent finding non-intuitive optimal sequences
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer dielectric multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band infrared transmission. Layer sequence: Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS (20 finite layers, strictly alternating Ge and ZnS starting with Ge). Wavelength bands: passbands at 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm (maximize transmittance), stopbands at 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm (minimize transmittance). Normal incidence, unpolarized light, coherent TMM. Initialize Ge layers at 550 nm (quarter-wave at 4.4 μm) and ZnS layers at 900 nm (quarter-wave at 4.4 μm). Optimization bounds: Ge [412, 688] nm (±25% of 550), ZnS [675, 1125] nm (±25% of 900). Use gradient_thickness optimizer with learning rate 0.001 (5x reduction from baseline), clamp thickness changes to ±15% of nominal values for first 3 epochs, enforce hard alternation constraint (odd layers must be Ge, even layers must be ZnS). Maximum 500 optimization iterations. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Directly addresses feedback directives (quarter-wave anchoring, ±15% step clamping, 5x learning rate reduction, alternation constraints) while testing whether iteration 09's failure was due to bound width rather than initialization principle. Preserves 20-layer topology from successful iteration 05.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:237542117 supports multi-cavity Fabry-Perot design for mid-IR bandpass filters with Ge/ZnS material pair, motivating route_01_refine_24layer's three-cavity topology
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:139773493 demonstrates computational optimization of multilayer designs from quarter-wave starting points, supporting all three routes' initialization strategies
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:288752787 shows bandwidth-selectivity tradeoffs in gas sensing filters, informing soft objective weighting for dual-band optimization
Prior iteration 05's 0.978 score with Ge/ZnS 20-layer design sets performance baseline; iteration 09's 0.383 score with quarter-wave seeding identifies over-constraint risk
unresolved_decisions: Whether three-cavity topology (24 layers) provides sufficient improvement over two-cavity (20 layers) to justify fabrication complexity
Whether ZnSe/ZnS material pair offers measurable absorption advantage over Ge/ZnS in 4-5 μm range without sacrificing index contrast
Optimal balance between quarter-wave analytical initialization and optimization bound width for convergence
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
